title: Universal Print: audit records in the Microsoft Purview unified audit log
summary: Hold: the statement that audit-record fields are undocumented is too broad. Microsoft documents the enclosing record's user, activity and object fields; the remaining gap is the Universal Print-specific payload. The roadmap facts and listed audit controls are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Universal Print audit records for administrator changes and user activities including print submissions and printer registrations.
claims.quote: I can access Universal Print audit records of key administrator and user activities, such as print job submissions, configuration changes, and printer registrations.

claims.claim: The planned records will be available in the Purview unified audit log for compliance and long-term record-keeping.
claims.quote: Audit records will be available in Microsoft Purview’s Unified Audit Log for compliance and long-term record-keeping.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions: record fields
claims.claim: The fields inside a Universal Print audit record, including user details, are not described.
claims.quote:
userId | String | The identifier of the user, system account, service, or application that performed the activity.
userPrincipalName | String | The user principal name of the user who performed the activity.
claims.fix: Replace the broad field-absence statements with 'The Universal Print-specific fields inside auditData.dynamicProperties are not described on the two Graph payload pages. The enclosing auditLogRecord documents common fields including operation, objectId, userId and userPrincipalName.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/security-auditlogrecord?view=graph-rest-1.0. Narrow the Open questions item to 'Which Universal Print-specific printer and document fields are carried inside auditData.dynamicProperties?'

claims.claim: The Microsoft services that support auditing page lists no Universal Print record type.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Universal Print audit record fields schema UniversalPrintManagement UniversalPrintPrintJob'. Opened Microsoft services that support auditing and searched Office 365 Management Activity API schema; the former has no Universal Print row, but the latter names both record types.
claims.fix: Keep the uncertainty about portal dropdown availability, but replace the supporting explanation with 'The services summary omits Universal Print, but the Office 365 Management Activity API schema lists UniversalPrintPrintJob (377) and UniversalPrintManagement (427); their availability in the portal dropdown is not stated.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-schema.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Searching through the Purview portal requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in that portal.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: Access to audit cmdlets requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Restricted administrators assigned administrative units can search and export user-generated logs only within those units.
claims.quote: A restricted admin can only search and export user-generated audit logs within the scope of their assigned administrative units.

claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators have access to all audit logs.
claims.quote: An unrestricted admin has access to all audit logs, including logs generated by non-user and system accounts.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The documented retention for users assigned non-E5 Office 365 or Microsoft 365 licences is 180 days.
claims.quote: For users assigned any other (non-E5) Office 365 or Microsoft 365 license, the system retains audit records for 180 days.

claims.claim: E5 users get one-year default retention for Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange and SharePoint activities, and Universal Print is not named in that default list.
claims.quote: the system retains audit records for Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, and SharePoint activity for one year by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing: Audit retention
claims.claim: An audit log retention policy permits retention of activities in other services for up to one year under the E5 retention provision.
claims.quote: Organizations can also create audit log retention policies to retain audit records for activities in other services for up to one year.
claims.fix: Clarify 'Other services need an audit log retention policy, up to one year' as 'For retention beyond 180 days and up to one year in other services, an audit log retention policy and an Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Purview Suite or E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on licence for the user generating the record are required.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-retention-policies. This is not an absolute one-year maximum: that page also documents longer retention with the 10-year add-on.

claims.claim: No separate UI or API switch for Universal Print records in the unified audit log is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Universal Print" "audit" "enable" "disable"'; 'Universal Print audit logging enable disable default tenant settings Graph print settings'. Read tenant settings and Graph printSettings excerpt; no audit switch. Logs and Alerting's switch sends different telemetry to Azure Monitor.

claims.claim: Turning unified auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled in Exchange Online PowerShell verifies auditing, with True indicating it is on.
claims.quote:
Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled
A value of True for the UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled property indicates that auditing is turned on.
